title: The Question I Finally Asked
script: Narrator: [uncertain] In my evening English class, I understood most lessons, but one grammar point confused me for three weeks.
Narrator: Each time the teacher asked whether we had questions, I looked down. Everyone else seemed ready to continue.
Narrator: [worried] I was afraid my question was too simple. I copied examples from the board and promised to study them alone.
Narrator: At home, the examples still made no sense. I completed exercises by guessing and felt more worried each week.
Narrator: One Tuesday, the teacher gave us a short task. I made the same mistake in every sentence.
Narrator: [gently] She did not criticize me. She placed a small mark beside the first answer and asked me to visit her desk after class.
Narrator: I expected a long explanation, but she used two colored pens and one clear example. Suddenly, I saw the difference.
Narrator: [relieved] Then she said that several students had made the same mistake. They had also been quiet when she invited questions.
Narrator: The next lesson, I raised my hand. My voice felt weak, yet I asked her to explain one instruction again.
Narrator: [nervous] Two classmates nodded with relief. One of them thanked me during the break because he had been confused too.
Narrator: That moment changed how I see questions. A question is not proof that a student is slow or unprepared.
Narrator: [thoughtful] It is information for the teacher. It shows where the lesson needs another example, a slower step, or different words.
Narrator: I still try to solve problems independently first. I read my notes and attempt the exercise.
Narrator: But if I remain confused, I now ask. Ten honest seconds in class can save an hour of guessing at home.
Narrator: [confident] Learning became easier when I stopped trying to look perfect and started trying to understand.

quiz.question: How long had the grammar point confused the narrator?
quiz.explanation: The narrator had remained confused for three weeks.

quiz.question: Why did she stay quiet?
options: She feared the question was too simple
quiz.explanation: She worried that others would think the question was simple.

quiz.question: How did the teacher explain the point?
options: With two colored pens and one clear example
quiz.explanation: A simple visual example made the difference clear.

quiz.question: How did classmates react when she later asked a question?
options: They showed relief because some were also confused
quiz.explanation: Other students had needed the explanation too.

quiz.question: What did the narrator learn?
options: Questions help teachers see what needs clarification
quiz.explanation: An honest question supports understanding for both learner and teacher.

quiz.question: What happened when the narrator guessed at home?
quiz.explanation: Guessing did not solve the grammar confusion.

quiz.question: What does “criticize” mean in this story?
options: Invite a student to a desk
quiz.explanation: The teacher did not shame the narrator for wrong answers.

quiz.question: Why were two classmates relieved?
quiz.explanation: The narrator’s question helped students who had stayed quiet.

quiz.question: When does the narrator ask for help now?
options: After trying notes and the exercise first
quiz.explanation: She first works independently, then asks if confusion remains.

quiz.question: What did asking one question save?
options: More time spent guessing at home
quiz.explanation: A brief question gave a faster path to understanding.
